Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:181152
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10543 of 2023

Applicant :- Veer Singh
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Nagendra Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant Veer Singh seeking anticipatory bail in Criminal Case No. 24649 of 2022, case crime no. 294 of 2022, under Sections 406, 419, 420 IPC,
Police Station Civil Lines, District Budaun.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of his arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
It is further submitted that nowhere in the F.I.R. it is mentioned as to when the money was paid to the present applicant by the informant.
It is also submitted that as per the statement of Tejpal, father of the informant, money was not paid to the present applicant but to the co-accused Updesh Kumar Vaishya.
It is further submitted that no amount has been deposited in the bank account of the applicant.
It is next submitted that the applicant has no criminal history to his credit.
The investigation of the case has been completed and charge sheet has been filed and applicant has been cooperative during course of Veer Singh vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 19 September, 2023

1 investigation.
It has been submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
The alleged offences are punishable with the imprisonment for a maximum period of seven years.
It is lastly submitted that co-accused Updesh Kumar Vaishya has been granted regular bail by the Court concerned.

4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that the informant has paid Rs. 65,000/- and subsequently a huge amount of money in instalments on several occasions has been paid and these facts have been clearly stated by the informant in the statement under Section 161 CrPC.
The dates and places where the money was given by the informant to the applicant have also been stated by him in his said statement.
It is also submitted that the co-accused was also paid money at the insistence of the present applicant.
The co-accused Updesh Kumar Vaishya has been granted regular bail by the Court concerned but the same has been granted giving him benefit of Section 437(2) CrPC.
During course of investigation, ample and sufficient evidence has been collected against the present applicant.

It is further submitted that when the money was paid to the present applicant, the informant had also made mobile video recording of the same and CDR has been handed over to the I.O. by the victim of the case.

It is also submitted that the present applicant is a person of criminal character and in all probabilities he would have taken money from several persons on the false pretext of providing employment to them, hence, custodial interrogation of the applicant is required in the matter.

5. The prosecution story, as unfolded in the F.I.R., is that on the pretext of providing some employment to the informant, the applicant had taken Rupees Two Lakhs in instalments and also involved an unknown person as a Senior Officer in Punjab National Bank but no job was provided to the applicant nor his money was repaid to him.
F.I.R. was lodged on 25.5.2022 and investigation started, which culminated into filing of the charge sheet.

6. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

7. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant, all attending facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that allegations are serious in nature, without expressing any Veer Singh vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179008951/
2 opinion on the merits of the case, in my view, it is not a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: Prayer made in the application is refused.
8. The application is rejected.

9. However, it is observed that the bail application of the applicant, if moved, shall be considered and decided by the Court concerned in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
